entity: Slovak merchants / acquirers (Act 384/2025 Z. z. cashless-acceptance mandate, as postponed by Act 30/2026 Z. z.)
signal: [STANDING — dated 2025/2026, re-checked this run] Act No. 384/2025 Z. z. on the recording of sales (o evidencii tržieb) obliges sellers to let the customer pay cashlessly on purchases ABOVE EUR 1, with sanctions for non-compliance. The commencement of that duty sits in § 19 ods. 5 of the Act, and it was POSTPONED from the originally legislated 01/03/2026 to 01/05/2026 by Act No. 30/2026 Z. z. (adopted 12/02/2026, published in the Zbierka zákonov 27/02/2026), which amended § 19 ods. 5 specifically. The law explicitly permits alternatives to a card terminal — notably a QR code scanned and paid from a mobile banking app, or any other payment method the seller chooses as suited to the point of sale — so it does NOT compel a POS terminal per merchant. The terminal-count movement carried from the baseline (70,943 to 77,711 POS terminals between 31/12/2025 and 31/05/2026, +9.5%) COULD NOT BE VERIFIED against NBS payment statistics this run and should be treated as unconfirmed. Nothing in the ÚVO Vestník relates to this mandate: it drives private merchant and acquirer purchasing, not public procurement.
source_name: Zbierka zákonov SR — zákon č. 384/2025 Z. z. § 15 / § 19 ods. 5, as amended by zákon č. 30/2026 Z. z. (slov-lex canonical page; corroborated via the Slovak Chamber of Tax Advisers, skdp.sk)
implies: The strongest Slovak demand driver for Printec's POS/softPOS and terminal-management lines, but it is realised entirely through acquirers and merchants and is invisible on ÚVO — consistent with the structural finding that Slovakia is a direct-sell market, not a tender market. The QR-payment carve-out caps the terminal upside: the smallest merchants can comply with no hardware at all, which favours softPOS (a payment terminal running as software on the merchant's own phone) plus a terminal-management system over classic Verifone/Castles boxes at the long tail. The now-firm 01/05/2026 in-force date means the enforcement ramp, not the compliance deadline, is the 2026-2027 sales trigger.
likelihood: In force since 01/05/2026 after the statutory postponement; enforcement ramp through 2026-2027
